title: Quantum 1-PCA with Pauli Measurements in Nearly Linear Time
abstract: We consider the problem of quantum 1-PCA: given copies of an unknown $n$-qubit mixed state, recover a classical description of its leading eigenvector. Our goal is to do so using non-adaptive and single-qubit measurements. For an $n$-qubit state with top eigenvalue $λ$ and spectral gap at least $Δ> 0$, we give an algorithm that recovers the leading eigenvector to fidelity at least $1 - \varepsilon$ with high probability using $\tilde{O}\left( {2^n \cdot η^2} / {Δ^3 \varepsilon^3}\right)$ copies and $\tilde{O}((2^n/Δ\varepsilon) \cdot \operatorname{poly}(η/Δ\varepsilon))$ time, where $η= \max (1 - λ, \varepsilon)$. All of our measurements are non-adaptively chosen, and performed in single-qubit Pauli bases. When the spectral gap is constant and the desired accuracy is comparable to the noise level, i.e. $\varepsilon = Ω(η)$, our runtime and copy complexity become $\tilde{O} (2^n / \varepsilon)$. This generalizes the guarantees of Grewal et al. [arXiv:2601.04444], who achieved similar rates, but under the assumption $η= 0$, i.e., that the state was pure. Our results show that the same rates hold in the presence of state misspecification, up to polylogarithmic factors. From a technical perspective, our algorithm works by recursively constructing low-dimensional subspaces that approximately preserve the target eigenvector. To achieve nearly linear runtime dependence on the dimension of the Hilbert space, we develop a novel structured Pauli sampling scheme that enables fast batched computation of exponentially many projected Pauli matrices.
summary: This work presents an efficient quantum algorithm for performing Principal Component Analysis on unknown $n$-qubit mixed states using only single-qubit Pauli measurements. By developing a structured Pauli sampling scheme and a recursive subspace projection method, the authors achieve near-optimal complexity bounds. This is significant for quantum characterization protocols where measurement resources are limited.
main_problem: The paper addresses the quantum Principal Component Analysis (PCA) problem: recovering a classical description of the leading eigenvector of an unknown $n$-qubit mixed state $ho$ using only non-adaptive, single-qubit Pauli measurements.
main_result: They provide an algorithm achieving near-optimal complexity, $	ilde{O}(2^n/\epsilon)$, for both copy count and runtime when the spectral gap is constant and accuracy matches noise levels. This generalizes prior work by handling mixed states.
method: The technique involves recursively constructing low-dimensional subspaces that approximate the target eigenvector, coupled with a novel structured Pauli sampling scheme for fast, batched computation of projected Pauli matrices.
model_or_system: The system is an unknown $n$-qubit mixed state $ho$. The analysis is rooted in quantum information theory, utilizing Pauli measurements to characterize the state's leading eigenvector.
key_observables: The leading eigenvector $|\psiangle$, the spectral gap $\Delta = \lambda - \lambda_2$, and the fidelity $|\langle\hat{\psi}|\psiangle|^2$.
important_parameters: The qubit number $n$, the target error $\epsilon$, and the noise parameter $\eta = \max(1 - \lambda, \epsilon)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on bounding error propagation across recursive subspace projections and assumes the existence of a structured Pauli sampling scheme for efficiency.
paper_structure: The paper details the overall algorithm (Algorithm 4) which iteratively prunes the state space. It builds upon techniques for estimating projected Pauli matrices using structured sampling and robust estimation methods like Lepskii's method.
why_interesting: The development of efficient, measurement-based algorithms for state characterization, particularly achieving near-exponential speedups in complexity, is crucial for practical quantum characterization protocols.
